Shrinking the Generation-Verification Gap with Weak Verifiers

paper.arxiv.2506.18203

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2506.18203v3. Weak-verifier aggregation and inference-call limitations establish verification/selection method scope. Table/prose and compute-unit inconsistencies remain qualified; no universal cost claim. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The aggregation model assumes conditional independence of verifier votes, and inference can require 30-plus verifier calls; on harder datasets with few correct candidate responses, selection remains difficult and is bounded by candidate generation.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Weaver uses weak supervision to weight multiple binary verifier signals for response selection; its setup allows a small labeled development subset, roughly 1% of test queries, to estimate global statistics.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The main evaluation generates 100 responses per query with Llama 3.3 70 B Instruct and combines a pool of 33 reward models and language-model judges; the paper compares selected-response accuracy with an oracle Pass@100 bound.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Table 1 reports average success rates across four tasks of 87.7% for Weaver, 72.2% for majority voting and 91.9% for oracle Pass@100; these are response-selection results under 100-generation conditions.
